question: Explain why Ohm's law is not regarded as a universal law. Give one condition under which it is valid.

options.A: Ohm's law is universal because $V/I$ is constant for every device at all temperatures.
options.B: Ohm's law is valid for all conductors provided the current is large enough.
options.C: Ohm's law is not universal because many devices have non-linear $V-I$ characteristics; it is valid for ohmic conductors when physical conditions, such as temperature, remain constant.
options.D: Ohm's law fails only because resistance becomes zero at constant temperature.
